data.title: SA Asks: Which software companies could be takeover targets?
data.description:
Last week, shares of Workday (WDAY) rallied on reports that the software company might be acquired by private equity firm Silver Lake.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Chris DeMuth Jr., The Value Investor, and Kevin Anthony D. Arroyo which software companies they thought could also be potential takeover targets.

Chris DeMuth Jr.: Activists are on a good run pressing managements to run reviews. It looks like Elliott will succeed with their Workday (WDAY) investment if it gets sold to Silver Lake. Next after that? Maybe Jana will get Alkami Technology (ALKT) sold. That process looks promising. 

(Chris DeMuth Jr. leads the SA investing group Sifting the World.) 

The Value Investor: In my view, businesses that are not too large, not too leveraged, and have real potential to use AI to their benefit are prime candidates. These include names like Atlassian (TEAM), Intuit (INTU), Paychex (PAYX), SS&C Technologies (SSNC), and Docusign (DOCU), but with the comment that many of these stocks have rebounded recently, thereby reducing the chance of M&A action.

(The Value Investor leads the SA investing group Value in Corporate Events.)

Kevin Anthony D. Arroyo: The debilitating effect of AI in the software industry, reflected in their valuations, could open the floodgates for incumbent companies to further consolidate their industry. Which is something that they have failed to do in the past due to antitrust concerns and private equity looking for cheap target companies with healthier balance sheets and solid franchises that could be levered up to generate attractive returns. 

The software companies that I find most susceptible to a takeover are the smaller ones that compete in specialized segments or verticals. Names include Monday.com (MNDY) in business management, Appian (APPN) in enterprise process automation, PTC (PTC) in product lifecycle management, Freshworks (FRSH) in ticketing and service management, and DocuSign (DOCU) in document and agreement management.

The bolt-on acquisition characteristics of some of these small companies are a perfect match with the more portfolio-driven business models of some of the big traditional software companies such as Adobe (ADBE), Autodesk (ADSK), and Salesforce (CRM). 

I see private equity going for bigger software companies with healthy balance sheets, established customer and distribution relationships, and a solid churn rate, as they would likely provide stable and resilient cash flows despite the potential disruption from AI.

data.title: Jupiter Neurosciences announces pricing of $2M registered direct offering

data.title: SA analyst upgrades/downgrades: AAPL, AAP, AMD, LOW
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) earned an upgrade to Buy from Future Stack Investment, fueled by explosive data center revenue growth tied to the AI infrastructure boom. Advance Auto Parts (AAP) also received a Buy upgrade from Seeking Profits following a sharp share price decline, with margin recovery viewed as underappreciated by the market.

On the downgrade front, Apple (AAPL) was cut to Sell by Bay Area Ideas amid valuation concerns and mounting margin pressures, while Lowe's (LOW) was downgraded to Hold by Albert Anthony despite delivering consecutive earnings beats, as housing market headwinds cloud the near-term outlook.

Upgrades

  • Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): Upgrade Hold to Buy by Future Stack Investment. The analyst highlights AMD's dramatic transformation in its data center business, with AI-related products now driving the majority of revenue and creating a powerful, self-reinforcing growth cycle.

"The valuation remains demanding, and it's not a low-risk Buy. Overall, I think the basic picture has strengthened substantially to the point where I'm convinced that the expected upside outweighs the valuation risk."

  • Advance Auto Parts (AAP): Upgrade to Buy by Seeking Profits. Following a 25% share price decline, the analyst sees significant opportunity in the company's underappreciated margin recovery and turnaround progress under new management.

"The auto parts retailer has undergone a meaningful transformation under new management, closing unprofitable stores, shedding noncore businesses, and improving the health of its balance sheet...With updated financials, now is a good time to see if the recovery thesis is broken or if the dramatic move has created an opportunity."

Downgrades

  • Apple (AAPL): Downgrade Hold to Sell by Bay Area Ideas. The analyst argues that Apple's valuation premium is no longer justified given decelerating growth, component cost pressures, and expected gross margin contraction in the coming quarter.

"Despite receding from the recent peak, Apple's forward P/E ratio is at a reading of 35.93. That represents a bit of expansion from the 34.10 reading that's found in my previous update. With the valuation having gotten more expensive but the outlook deteriorating for the company, I believe that the risk/reward setup has now become bearish."

  • Lowe's Companies (LOW): Downgrade Buy to Hold by Albert Anthony. Despite another earnings beat and strong online sales growth, the analyst cites challenging margin trends and sector headwinds from a sluggish housing market as reasons for a more cautious stance.

"Market momentum has not been too confident on this stock since around springtime, and it continues to severely underperform a major benchmark like the S&P 500, without a sign of a recovery emerging. So, I don't expect it to achieve alpha anytime soon, and this hurts any confidence in a bull case."

data.title: Charter closes Cox deal, sees potential for $1 billion in annual synergies
data.description:
Charter Communications (CHTR) has completed its $34.5 billion acquisition of Cox Communications, expanding its Spectrum footprint to 45 states and creating a larger broadband, video, and mobile operator.

The transaction, announced on Thursday, brings Cox’s operations into Charter’s (CHTR) network and gives the company additional opportunities to expand its product offerings and customer relationships. Spectrum plans to roll out its full suite of products, including its pricing and packaging, across former Cox markets in mid-September. Cox internet customers who do not already use Cox Mobile will receive a year of free mobile service.

The deal could also provide a lift through cost savings. On Charter’s (CHTR) second-quarter earnings call, CEO Chris Winfrey said the company continues to expect at least $800 million of annual run-rate transaction expense synergies from the Cox combination, while suggesting the figure could ultimately reach $1 billion.

Charter (CHTR) has also set a post-transaction leverage target of 3.5 times, which it expects to reach within three years following the Cox and Liberty Broadband transactions.

The transaction leaves about $12 billion of Cox debt and finance leases at Charter (CHTR) subsidiaries. Cox Enterprises received Charter securities and cash and now holds about 26% of the combined company on a fully diluted, as-converted basis.

Charter (CHTR) will continue to operate its services under the Spectrum name, although the parent company plans to adopt the Cox Communications name within a year.

Shares were up about 3% in the afternoon trade on Friday.

data.title: Centrus Energy CEO sees U.S. military as new market for company's enriched uranium
data.description:
Centrus Energy (LEU) up 4% in Friday's trading as CEO Amir Vexler said he sees a new market for the company's enriched uranium coming from the U.S. military through a potential supply deal to meet domestic security needs.

Vexler told Bloomberg in an interview that he anticipates a U.S. government contract to supply nuclear fuel for defense will be finalized this year, after the Department of Energy issued a notice of intent last year to award the sole-source contract to Centrus (LEU), the only U.S.-owned company that produces enriched uranium for reactors.

An agreement could include supplying fuel for U.S. Navy vessels or small reactors the military plans to deploy at bases, Vexler said, adding the supply could also support production of tritium, which is used to make nuclear weapons, although the CEO emphasized that end uses would be determined by the DoE's National Nuclear Security Administration.

Centrus (LEU), which is building out a multibillion-dollar enrichment facility in Ohio to supply uranium fuel for both conventional nuclear plants and next-generation reactors, has a competitive edge in the national security market because of restrictions on using uranium sourced abroad for U.S. military applications, Vexler said.

"You basically have to be an American company," the CEO said. "The only production-ready technology that has that is Centrus' enrichment process."

data.title: Dutch Bros goes on the autumn offensive
data.description:
Dutch Bros (BROS) is not sitting out the fall pumpkin drink season after it brought back its popular Caramel Pumpkin Brûlée and Cookie Butter drinks, as well as unveiling a new Autumn Berry drink for the first time. The three drinks are now available at all Dutch Bros (BROS) locations while supplies last.

Caramel Pumpkin Brûlée and Cookie Butter arrived on the menu a day earlier than last year, when they were a traffic driver for Dutch Bros. (BROS) in parts of Q3 and Q4.

"Our customers absolutely loved Caramel Pumpkin Brûlée and Cookie Butter, so naturally, we had to bring them back," highlighted Dutch Bros Chief Marketing Officer Tana Davila.

Dutch Bros (BROS) trades about 25% below where the restaurant stock stood six weeks ago. Wall Street analysts have a consensus Buy rating on BROS, while Seeking Alpha analysts are more cautious with a consensus Hold rating.

data.title: Neocloud Nscale looking to raise up to $3B in US IPO: report
data.description:
British neocloud provider Nscale is looking to raise up to $3B in its U.S. IPO, Bloomberg News reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

London-based Nscale, which provides a full-stack AI cloud platform and is backed by Nvidia (NVDA), is heading for an IPO that could take place as soon as September, the report added.

Discussions are ongoing, and details of the IPO plan could change and the listing could be delayed, the report noted.

Nscale did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's request for comment.

Last month, it was reported that Nscale is working with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan on the IPO. The company competes against other neoclouds such as Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV) and IREN (IREN).

The company is developing data centers in sites including Norway and West Virginia and has told prospective investors it has around $51B of total contracted revenue ahead of the listing, as per a prior report. 

Nscale’s board includes former Meta executives Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg, who previously served as the U.K.'s deputy prime minister.

Last month, Nscale announced plans to acquire Anyscale, a San Francisco-based software firm that scales AI workloads. The deal is reportedly valued at about $1.65B. The company is also planning to spend €695M (about $812M) on infrastructure in Portugal under an expansion of its collaboration with Microsoft (MSFT).

data.title: Quantum stocks surge after Q2 results show significant improvement
data.description:
Quantum stocks across the board were leaping on Friday as market participants took advantage of the long-term opportunity they might provide.

The most recent wave of earnings reports from quantum computing companies demonstrated substantial year-over-year revenue gains from several firms.

D-Wave (QBTS) climbed 7% by noon trading after the company received an Outperform rating and $35 price target from BMO Capital Markets. The company utilizes annealing and gate-model systems.

"Having both technologies allows QBTS to address different quantum applications and unlock the full TAM potential," said BMO analyst Harsh Kumar in an investor note. "D-Wave has an addressable market opportunity of $450-850 billion, based on estimates from BCG. Within this, annealing is about $100-220 billion and the rest from gate model."

D-Wave is one of the few quantum companies that generates commercial revenue from its annealing quantum computers. BMO expects them to begin offering customers access to its gate-based systems by 2028 as it also pursues commercialization of complete quantum systems. D-Wave has sold two quantum systems this year, and it anticipates selling two to three complete systems per year starting in 2027.

On Wednesday, IBM (IBM) revealed it had "successfully" joined and cooled down two cryogenic modules into a single environment, an important milestone on its path to creating the world's first fault-tolerant quantum computer. IBM ticked up 2% on Friday.

Rigetti (RGTI) had jumped 9% by noon trading. Its second-quarter earnings results demonstrated progress as system and component sales totaled $4.1M compared to zero during the same quarter one year prior.

Meanwhile, Quantum Computing (QUBT) leaped 8%. Its second-quarter results featured revenue of $5.6M compared to the $65,000 it produced a year earlier and $3.7M for the quarter prior.

"Looking ahead, we remain focused on two complementary growth engines," said Quantum Computing CEO Yuping Huang during the earnings call. "First, we will continue to move aggressively along our quantum technology road map, leveraging our differentiated room temperature photonic architecture to develop quantum systems that are smaller, more scalable, and more practical for real-world deployment. As these technologies become commercially viable, it allows us to better serve our existing customer base, who will be exploring use cases for these systems."

"Second, we will continue to grow our commercial portfolio of photonic components, lasers, detectors, photonic integrated circuits, thin-film lithium niobate technologies, optical packaging, advanced packaging, semiconductor manufacturing, and other foundry services," he added.

IQM Quantum Computers (IQMX) popped up 7% on Friday. Its second-quarter revenue increased 27% year over year to $7.8M. It now expects full-year revenue of $49M to $55M. IQM went public in late June.

Infleqtion (INFQ), another quantum company that went public earlier this year, surged 9% by early afternoon trading. Its most recent earnings boasted a 112% year-over-year revenue jump.

IonQ (IONQ) increased 7.5%. Earlier this week, it revealed a new partnership with the Canadian Microelectronics Corporation to expand quantum computing access to Canada-based researchers and businesses.

data.title: BJ's raises FY2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $4.60-$4.80 while maintaining 2%-3% comp guidance
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: BJ's Wholesale Club (BJ) Q2 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • “Net sales were up nearly 16% year-over-year and merchandise comps grew 3.1% with traffic accelerating during the quarter.” (President, CEO & Chairman Robert Eddy) He added, “This marks our 18th consecutive quarter of traffic growth and our 15th consecutive quarter of market share gains.”

  • Eddy highlighted category performance, stating, “Our perishables, grocery and sundries division delivered solid comp growth of 2.8% in the quarter, led by grocery,” and “Our General Merchandise and Services division sustained comp growth of 5.3% in the quarter.” He also emphasized fuel, saying, “Comp gallons were up double digits, accelerating from the strong results we saw in Q1,” and that “fuel profit dollars ahead of plan… was a meaningful contributor to our overall results.”

  • Eddy framed member momentum as central to the model: “We reached a new milestone of 8.5 million members this quarter,” and said “Membership fee income grew nearly 10% year-over-year.” He also described digital engagement: “Digitally enabled comp sales grew 30% in the quarter,” and added, “Bev, our AI-powered shopping assistant, is live and gaining momentum… now had over 100,000 conversations with members.”

  • Eddy detailed unit and price-gap positioning, stating, “Traditional grocers have been raising prices,” and “units growing more than 300 basis points faster than the market in the quarter.” He also outlined expansion progress: “In the second quarter, we opened three new clubs in Texas,” and said, “We have 7 additional club openings and one relocation planned for the remainder of the year.”

  • “Net sales in the second quarter were $6.1 billion… Membership fee income grew 9.9% to $136 million… Adjusted EBITDA increased 14.3% to $347 million and adjusted EPS was $1.36.” (Executive VP & CFO Laura Felice)

Outlook

  • “We are maintaining our full year guidance of 2% to 3% comparable club sales growth, excluding gasoline.” (CFO Felice)

  • “For adjusted EPS, we are raising our range and now expect $4.60 to $4.80 for the full year, reflecting the strong results we delivered in the second quarter, particularly in our gas business.” (CFO Felice)

  • Compared with last quarter’s guidance language, management moved the adjusted EPS range higher from “$4.40 to $4.60” while keeping the comp outlook “2% to 3% comparable club sales growth, excluding gasoline.” (CFO Felice, Q1 vs. Q2 transcripts)

Financial Results

  • “Total comparable club sales increased 11.9% and excluding the impact of gasoline sales, merchandise comparable sales increased 3.1%,” with “Inflation… just under 1 point in the quarter.” (CFO Felice)

  • “Gross profit increased 10.3% to $1. $11 billion,” while “merchandise gross margin rate decreased approximately 20 basis points year-over-year.” (CFO Felice)

  • Fuel and share trends were a notable earnings driver: “Comp gallons increased 10.5%,” and “industry data indicates overall comp fuel gallons declined by approximately 5% during the period.” (CFO Felice)

  • Cash and capital deployment commentary emphasized flexibility: “adjusted free cash flow of $266 million,” “net leverage of 0.5 turns,” and “We repurchased $124 million of shares… approximately $422 million remaining under our existing repurchase authorization.” (CFO Felice)

Q&A

  • Edward Kelly, Wells Fargo: asked how tariff refund and fuel strength are reinvested; President, CEO & Chairman Eddy said, “we… had the tariff refunds… and we’re just about through those,” and added investment is aimed at “long-term lifetime value,” not “returns within one particular quarter.”

  • Edward Kelly, Wells Fargo: asked about opex and the sale-leaseback magnitude; CFO Felice said the gain was “about $11 million to the P&L.”

  • Peter Benedict, Baird: pressed on why MFI growth stayed near 10% despite fee-increase lapping; CEO Eddy cited “a fantastic renewal rate performance,” “about 43% of our membership in higher tier members,” and reiterated the company still expects growth to “slide down to about 6% at the end of the year.”

  • Katharine McShane, Goldman Sachs: asked if price investments can persist without tariff refunds; CEO Eddy said, “the worry that margin rates will decline precipitously… is misplaced,” citing “other places to source funding,” including “working with our suppliers,” “retail media,” and gas.

  • Michael Baker, D.A. Davidson: asked for Texas color; EVP Strategy & Development William Werner said Texas is showing “outside membership gains” and strong early engagement, with “more to come,” including “our club in Mesquite later this year” and “our next club in Tyler… for early next year.”

  • Charles Grom, Gordon Haskett: asked about SKU rationalization; CEO Eddy said, “our goal really is to take about 20% of our SKUs out over the next couple of years,” moving legacy clubs from “about 7,500” toward “about 6,000, 6,500 SKUs.”

  • Steven Zaccone, Citigroup: asked what drove the EPS raise and whether 2H changed; CFO Felice said, “the raise on EPS… is a result largely of our gas business,” and characterized the approach as “taking the beat and raising on it.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical, concentrating on durability of pricing investments, membership fee income sustainability, margin cadence without tariff refunds, and the drivers behind the raised EPS outlook (e.g., “how do you think about… lapping them when there aren’t necessarily tariff refunds,” Goldman Sachs).

  • Management tone was positive and confident in prepared remarks, emphasizing “strong second quarter” momentum, and in Q&A leaned on funding flexibility and long-term returns, with CEO Eddy stating, “the worry… is misplaced,” and repeatedly framing reinvestment around “lifetime value.”

  • Versus Q1, the discussion shifted from planning around tariff refunds and volatile gas margins to explaining an EPS guide increase “particularly in our gas business,” alongside more detailed initiatives (SKU reduction target and AI assistant usage). (Q1 vs. Q2 transcripts)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Guidance changed primarily on earnings: Q2 raised full-year adjusted EPS to “$4.60 to $4.80,” while Q1 guided “$4.40 to $4.60,” and both calls maintained “2% to 3% comparable club sales growth, excluding gasoline.” (CFO Felice)

  • Strategic emphasis broadened from Q1’s introduction of the new Chief Merchandising Officer and tariff-funded price investments to Q2’s operating detail on CMP/SKU reduction (“take about 20% of our SKUs out”) and explicit digital/AI traction (“over 100,000 conversations”). (CEO Eddy)

  • Analyst focus stayed consistent on tariffs, price investments, margins, gas, and Texas expansion, but Q2 added more probing on EPS bridge and the durability of investments after refunds taper. (Q1 vs. Q2 Q&A)

Risks and Concerns

  • Management flagged funding transition risk as tariff refunds fade: CEO Eddy said refunds are “just about through,” while emphasizing, “we’ve identified other places to source funding.”

  • CFO Felice cautioned on membership fee income growth normalization: “we continue to expect MFI growth to moderate throughout the year as the impact of last year’s fee increase normalizes.”

  • Consumer backdrop remains uneven: CEO Eddy said “the K-shaped economy persists,” adding that “the vast majority of our growth continues to be driven by our higher income members.”

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q2 as a quarter driven by accelerating traffic, sustained market share gains, and fuel outperformance, while framing reinvestment in price and member value as a long-term strategy funded by multiple levers beyond tariff refunds. The company maintained its full-year ex-gas comp outlook, raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance on gas strength, and highlighted expansion momentum—especially in Texas—along with a multi-year merchandising initiative to reduce SKU count by about 20% and continued growth in digitally enabled sales and member engagement tools.

data.title: Amazon Prime investing $2B in Latin America programming
data.description:
Amazon’s (AMZN) Prime Video plans to invest more than $2B in Latin American programming between 2027 and 2030, including live sporting events, original programs, and acquired content locally produced and acquired across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, and Chile.

The announcement was made on Thursday at Prime Video Presents Latin America, the company's inaugural regional showcase event in Mexico City. 

"What's happening in Latin America right now is extraordinary—the talent, the stories, the audiences," said Kelly Day, vice president of international at Prime Video.

The initiative will more than double the number of originals produced locally, with more than 24 new titles in 2027.

Prime Video also announced that later this year customers in Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Paraguay, and Peru will be able to subscribe to third-party streaming services directly through the Prime Video app.

In sports, Prime Video will become the new home for the Mexico National Team, airing 38 home soccer matches over four years beginning September 26.
